chunks: From him, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah.
He said: I asked him about a man who comes upon a dead animal in the water.
Then he said: He performs wudu from the side where the dead animal is not.

key_terms.النَّاحِيَةِ: side/direction — the spatial qualifier that determines the valid point of purification
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water — the purifying medium under jurisprudential examination here
key_terms.الْمَيْتَةُ: maytah — dead animal carcass (not slaughtered per Islamic rite), a source of ritual impurity (najasah)
key_terms.يَتَوَضَّأُ: performs wudu — ritual ablution required before salat

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia jurisprudential ruling on performing wudu when a dead animal (maytah) is present in the water?
ai.summary: Sama'ah narrates his question to the Imam (likely Imam al-Sadiq AS) about a man who encounters a dead animal (maytah) in a body of water. The Imam rules that wudu remains valid if performed from the side of the water uncontaminated by the carcass, preserving ritual purity while enabling valid worship.
